name: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome due to 11p15 Microduplication

criteria.description: Abdominal wall defects such as omphalocele or umbilical hernia
Molecular confirmation of 11p15 microduplication affecting imprinting centers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular confirmation of 11p15 microduplication plus at least one major clinical feature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic confirmation due to phenotypic overlap with other imprinting disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic enlarged tongue causing feeding and respiratory difficulties
Asymmetric overgrowth of one side of the body or limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal wall defects (omphalocele or umbilical hernia)
searchTerms: belly wall defect with organs outside

common.notes: Low blood sugar episodes in the neonatal period

searchTerms: folds or pits on outer ear
ear creases or small indentations near ear

common.notes: Includes hepatomegaly, nephromegaly, and pancreatic enlargement
searchTerms: big liver, spleen, or other organs

occasional.notes: Enlargement of the heart observed in some cases

searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth

occasional.notes: Structural anomalies such as nephromegaly or cysts

laboratory: Neonatal hypoglycemia detected by blood glucose testing
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound or MRI detecting abdominal wall defects
MRI or CT for tumor surveillance
genetic: Microduplication at chromosome 11p15 affecting imprinting centers IC1 and/or IC2
Exclusion of other BWS molecular subtypes (e.g., loss of methylation, paternal uniparental disomy)
other: Physical examination revealing macroglossia and hemihyperplasia
Tumor screening protocols including abdominal ultrasound and serum markers

distinguishingFeatures: Molecular subtype differences (loss of methylation or paternal UPD rather than microduplication)
Variable presence of macroglossia and hemihyperplasia
Distinct facial features and skeletal anomalies
Presence of polydactyly and supernumerary nipples

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging abdominal mass suggestive of Wilms tumor
Persistent neonatal hypoglycemia refractory to treatment
Severe macroglossia causing airway obstruction or feeding difficulties
references: Weksberg R, Shuman C, Beckwith JB. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2010;18(1):8-14.
Brioude F, et al. Expert consensus document: Clinical and molecular diagnosis, screening and management of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2018;14(4):229-249.
